answer_text: Yes, by the state's own account. Colorado says that on Nov 18 an unauthorized user accessed myColorado platform data, and it shut the app down. It estimates roughly 100,000 users' data was involved. The app is still offline.
label: Confirmed

question_text: What data was accessed, and will I be told if mine was?
answer_text: The state says it was mainly documents users uploaded, such as photos or PDFs of passports, vehicle registrations and insurance cards, not payment information. It now expects to start telling affected users on Nov 30; it had said Nov 27.
label: Confirmed

what_would_settle_it: The state or law enforcement naming the attacker or describing the vulnerability.

question_text: When will the myColorado app be back?
what_would_settle_it: The state announcing on myColorado.gov that the app is back online.

question_text: Is the myColorado incident part of a wider attack on governments?
answer_text: Not as far as anyone has shown. The state says it has no reason to believe it is part of a bigger attack. Other government incidents the same week have not been linked to it.
label: Reported

question_text: Can I still use my Colorado digital ID or travel with it?
answer_text: Use your physical license or state ID, including at the airport. Some phones still show the cached digital ID in airplane mode, but the state asks people to carry the physical card.
label: Confirmed

question_text: How many people's documents were accessed in the myColorado incident?
what_would_settle_it: The state's count once it has matched the accessed documents to users, or the notices it expects to send from Nov 30.
